On the day of his daughter's birth James deposits \$1500 in a trust fund that pays interest of 3% p.a. compounded annually. He continues to deposit \$1500 in the trust fund on his daughter's birthday each year.

The amount, $A_n$, in the account immediately prior to the deposit being made on his daughter's $n^{\text{th}}$ birthday can be determined using the recurrence relation:

$$A_n=\left(A_{n-1}+1500\right)\left(1.03\right)$$

Where $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ and $A_0=0$.

Use the recurrence relation to find the amount of money in the trust fund immediately before James makes the deposit on his daughter's third birthday.

solutions.question: 1(a)
solutions.latex:
$a=2x$, $r=-10x$.

$T_n=2x\times(-10x)^{n-1}=2(-10)^{n-1}x^n$.

The power of 10 is one less than the power of $x$. When $n$ is even, $(-1)^{n-1}$ is negative. So the answer is D.

solutions.question: 2(c)
solutions.latex:
$0=640000\times1.004^n-250\times4000\left(1.004^n-1\right)$

$0=640000\times1.004^n-1000000\times1.004^n+1000000$

$360000\times1.004^n=1000000$

$1.004^n=\dfrac{25}{9}$

$n\ln(1.004)=\ln\left(\dfrac{25}{9}\right)$

$n=\dfrac{\ln\left(\frac{25}{9}\right)}{\ln(1.004)}=255.923\ldots$

It will take Andrew 256 months to repay the loan.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: establishing $1.004^n=\frac{25}{9}$; 1: correct answer (no penalty for rounding)

solutions.question: 4(a)
solutions.latex:
As $A$ and $B$ are independent, $P(A)=P(A\mid B)$.

$P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{|A\cap B|}{|B|}$, so $\dfrac{x+2}{x+12}=\dfrac27$.

$7x+14=2x+24$, $5x=10$, $x=2$.

Answer B.

Alternative: $P(A\cap B)=P(A)\times P(B)$ gives $\dfrac{2}{x+12}=\dfrac{x+2}{x+12}\times\dfrac{7}{x+12}$, so $\dfrac27=\dfrac{x+2}{x+12}$, $x=2$.

solutions.question: 4(c)
solutions.latex:
$P(W)+P(LLW)+P(LLLLW)+\ldots=\dfrac14+\left(\dfrac34\right)^2\times\dfrac14+\left(\dfrac34\right)^4\times\dfrac14+\ldots$

Geometric series with $a=\dfrac14$, $r=\left(\dfrac34\right)^2$.

$S_\infty=\dfrac{a}{1-r}=\dfrac{\frac14}{1-\left(\frac34\right)^2}=\dfrac47$

The probability Jo will eventually win is $\dfrac47$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: recognition of geometric series; 1: correct answer
